regime_context: Detector shows a broad, two-speed precious-metals leadership structure in Canada: Gold Miners lead by a wide margin with strong durable trend health and full breadth, Silver & Royalties trail as challenger, and Base Metals is the lone crowded complex. The absolute-trend gate is validated for risk control on this market, so eligible themes carry a staying-power filter — but cross-sectional rank is display-only context, not a return forecast.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Silver & Royalties can close the gap on Gold Miners — a confirmed handoff would show Silver's rank score within 0.3 of Gold's while keeping breadth above 0.8; if the margin stays above 0.5 for three more weeks, retire this watch.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners sit at the top of the ranks with the highest durability bar (0.85), a trend hurst tag, and full breadth (1.0) — the only theme showing clean trend health with no crowding flag. The absolute-trend gate is the one validated leg here, and this theme passes it most decisively. I lean overweight as a trend-continuation expression of prevailing leadership, not as a return forecast.
evidence: absolute_trend_gate validated as risk control (gate_helps true)
theses.dissent: Precious metals leadership can persist on narrative reflexivity long after fundamentals stall, and the 0.95 crowding_z is close to the flag zone — a slow bleed or sharp shake-out in gold prices would hit this theme hardest given its dominant weight.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO lags the S&P/TSX by 4% or more over any rolling 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties ranks second with a solid durability bar (0.77), full breadth, and no crowding flag. It shares the same precious-metals complex as the leader but is not crowded, making it a cleaner secondary expression of the metals narrative if gold leadership persists.
theses.dissent: Silver is more industrial-exposed than gold and more volatile; if the metals bid is purely a gold-safe-haven story, silver underperforms and the theme lags the leader without offering diversification.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO proxy underperforms XGD.TO proxy for Gold Miners by 3% over any 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals & Copper ranks third but carries the only crowding flag in the complex (crowding_z 1.23, crowded true) with a mixed hurst tag and lower durability than the precious metals leaders. Per the guardrails, crowding is a size-down caution, not a fade — but with a crowded flag in a theme already subordinate in the ranks, I would avoid adding fresh exposure here.
theses.dissent: Copper has independent demand drivers (electrification, grid capex) that can decouple from precious metals; if industrial metals rally on their own, avoiding this theme forfeits that beta.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO outperforms XGD.TO by 3% or more over any 10-day window before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
